18:5041*1978 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FOOTWEAR AND STATIONERY EYELETS 

(First Revision) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 10 March 1978, after the draft finalized by the 
Fasteners for Consumer Goods Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Consumer Products and Medical Instiuments Division Council. 

0.2 Footwear and stationery eyelets are used for providing reinforcement 
for lace-holes and also for securing two or more layers of materials 
together. A number of fancy shapes of eyelets is available but in this 
standard most popular round-shaped eyelets have only been covered. 

0.3 This standard was first issued in 1969. The present revision has been 
taken up in the light of the comments received on the standard. In this 
revision dimensions which are considered necessary from the manufactur- 
ing point of view have been included 

0.4 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from 
IND/GS/1365 'Eyelets boots black, eyelets boots brown ', issued by the 
Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 

0.5 This standard contains clauses 6.2, 7,3, 8.1 and 10,1 which call for 
agreement between the purchaser and thq supplier, and which permit the 
purchaspi to use his option for selection to suit his requirements. 

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS . 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements for footwear and stationery 

eyelets ( lound-shapcd ). 

♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ) 

3 



IS X 5041 - 1978 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 

2.1 Eyelet — A metal reinforcement for edges surrounding a hole in 
materials, such as textiles, leather, rubber, paper, plastics or combination 
thereof. 

2.2 Eyeletting — Setting and clenching of the eyelets to the required 
material. 

3. TYPES 

3.1 The eyelets shall have two types, namely. Type I and Type II 
depending upon the thickness of material as indicated in Tables 1 and 2. 

4. MATERIALS 

4.1 Eyelets shall be made from either of the following matciials: 

a) Brass sheet or strip conforming to Designation CuZn37 or CuZnSO 
of IS :410-I967», 

b) Aluminium sheet or strin conforming to Designation 19000 or 
31000 of IS : 737-1974t, and 

c) Carbon steel strip of dead soft temper conforming to IS : 4030- 

1973$. 

5. SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

5.1 The shape and dimensions of footwear and stationery eyelets shall be 
as shown in Tables 1 and 2. 

5*1.1 The starting thickness of sheet or strip shall be as given in 
Tables 1 and 2. A deviation of ±002 mm shall be allowed for brass 
sheet or strip, and j^oos^nm shall be allowed for aluminium sheet or 
strip. 

5.1.2 A deviation of ±0'1 mm shall be allowed on all dimensions 
wherever not mentioned. 

6. MANUFACTURE 

6.1 Eyelets shall be drawn to shape and size as shown in Tables 1 and 2. 
The free end of the shank of the steel and brass eyelets shall have eight 
equal splits while that of aluminium eyelets shall be without splits. The 
free end of the eyelets ( 1*5 to 2 mm in length ) shall be slightly curved 
inwards fur easy entry into the material. The shank of the eyelets may 
avc a taper of ^ 5 . 

♦Specification for rolled brass plate, sheet, strip and foil ( second revision ). 

tSpecificaiion for wrought aluminium and aluminium alloys, sheet and strip { for 
general engineering purposes ) ( second revision ), 

tSpecificaiion for cold roUed carbon steel strip for general engineering puiposes 
( second r4vision ) .

iPags 7, clause 7.3^ fifth sentence) - Substitute 
the following for the exAeting sentence: 

'In case of painted eyelets, the paint shall not 
peel or chip off during or after clenching or when

(CPDC 22) 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, IncJid 



IS : 5041 - 1978 

6*2 Aluminium eyelets may be provided with washers if required by the 
purchaser. The washers shall have internal diameter to suit the shank of 
eyelets and external diameter equal to the outer diameter of the flange 
of eyelets. The washers shall be made from 0"45 -f 003 mm or 
0'45 — 0*05 mm thick aluminium sheet. 

6.3 Maximum reduction due to forming shall not exceed 0'05 mm when 
measured anywhere on the periphery of the lip. 

7. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

7.1 The eyelets shall be well drawn out, and free from cracks, wrinkles, 
burrs, dents and other surface defects. 

7.2 The head and the shank of the eyelets shall be symmetrical to the 
centre line. 

7.3 The brass eyelets shall be finished bright. Aluminium eyelets shall 
be chemically passivatcd in alkaline chromate bath with dull grey finish 
unless otherwise specified by the purchaser. Steel eyelets shall be brass 
or nickel plated if required by the purchaser. The rim of the eyelets 
may be covered by paint, if required by the purchaser. When painted, 
the paint shall adhere firmly and shall not peel or chip off when subjected 
to adhesion test. The paint shall withstand a temperature oflSO'^Cfor 
one hour without discolouration. 

8. SAMPLING 

8.1 Sampling and acceptance criteria shall be as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier, A recommended scheme for the same is 
given in Appendix A. 

9. TEST 

9.1 The eyelets shall be clenched on leather, cardboard or any other 
suitable material of such thickness so as to leave 1*5 to 2 mm of the 
shank of the eyelets projecting ( see Fig. I ) using suitable clenching tool 
for spreading or rolling. The eyelets shall not show any sign of damage 
or distortion after the clenching operation. 

10. PACKING 

10.1 The eyelets shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier. 

11. MARKING 

ll.l The packet containing eyelets shall be clearly and indelibly marked 
with the manufacturer's namCj initials or trade-mark, type and the country 
of manufacture.

NoTR — The use of ihc TSI Certification Mark is governed by the provisioDi of 
ihc Indian Standaids InstituHon ( Ceriifiration Maiks ) Act and the Rules and 
Regulations made thereunder. Ihc li^I Mark on products covered by an Indian 
Standard conveys the assuiance t}iat they have been produced to comply with the 
requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the 
producer, TSI marked products arc also continuously checked by ISI for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence 
for the use of the Ibl Certificanon Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 



APPENDIX A 

{Clause 8,1 ) 

SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 
FOR FOOTWEAR AND STATIONERY EYELETS 

A-1. SCALE OF SAMPLING 

A-1.1 Lot — In any constijnment, all the eyelets manufactured from the 
same material under similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped 
together to constitute a lot. 

A<^1*1.1 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of 
this specification, test samples shall be exammed from each lot separately 
and shall be drawn at random from the lot in accordance with IS : 4905- 
1968*. 

A-2* SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

A-2.1 For workmanship and finish ( see 7.1 and 7-3 ), test { see 9 ) and 
dimensional requirements, the sampling plan with Inspection Level 
III and acceptable quality level 2'5, percent given in Tables 1 and 2 
respectively of IS ; 2500 ( Part I )-1973t shall be followed.
